LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY: POETRY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry, part of Strand 6 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we read poems fluently? 2. Why are poems important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension.

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment.

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. practice reading poems on animal welfare with correct pace and intonation,

2. watch poem recitations based on the theme from digital platforms,

3. work jointly with peers to compose simple poems based on the theme,

4. recite the poems in class while recording pace of recitation,

5. peer assess each other’s performance for improvement,

6. work jointly to answer questions from the poems,

7. team up to take part in a spoken word competition applying pace and intonation correctly,

8. record themselves reciting the spoken word and organise their work in digital portfolios. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. practice reading poems on animal welfare with correct pace and intonation,
2. watch poem recitations based on the theme from digital platforms,
3. work jointly with peers to compose simple poems based on the theme,
4. recite the poems in class while recording pace of recitation,
5. peer assess each other’s performance for improvement,
6. work jointly to answer questions from the poems,
7. team up to take part in a spoken word competition applying pace and intonation correctly,
8. record themselves reciting the spoken word and organise their work in digital portfolios. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creative thinking and imagination: This is developed as the learner embraces ideas that inspire creativity when taking part in

a spoken word competition applying pace and intonation.

• Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner interacts with technology as they record themselves reciting the spoken

word pieces.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is acquired as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when organising their spoken word recordings in

digital portfolios.

• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner accommodates each other’s opinion when peer assessing performances for

improvement.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Animal welfare: This is promoted as the learner accesses information on animals from various sources for information.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on taking care of animals to the concept of care for creation in Religious Education.
